brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Three full-height cells at level 0 supporting level 1 with solid top covers on all three level-1 cells (cover:0,0,1;full;top, cover:-1,0,1;full;top, cover:1,-1,1;full;top) forming continuous shelf decks; props book-stack and book-row placed on shelves visible in look.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: Configurator checks fit/collisions only; parts are 3D-printed plastic in user-chosen material. No tool here verifies load rating, strength, or 50 kg capacity. Built form provides shelf surfaces but cannot be claimed as 50 kg rated.
Two drawer parts added: drawer:0#1,-2#cut on piece:1,-2,0;half-n and drawer:0#-2,0#cut on piece:-2,0,0;half-n, both on half bases at ground level.

finish.summary: Built a 5-base shelf unit with 3 upper shelf surfaces and two half-base drawers at opposite ends, capped and joint-bolted, staged with books. 50 kg rating cannot be verified in this system and is marked unmet.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Your shelf with two drawers is next — I'll set up a configuration that holds your books while noting the 50kg rating can't be certified in plastic alone.

result.note: A drawer sits on the cut face of a half base: place a half base first. Half-n and half-s take any drawer style; half-e and half-w take a slide, swing or long drawer (find_sockets offers those once the half base is on). No place on the build takes this part right now. Change the build so it can (for example add the cells it needs beside or below it), then ask again. Guessing raw ops for a part with no offers rarely works.
Ask again with a family or a few words (text) to see the parts themselves.

events.text: I've got the plan for your drawer unit — now I'll assemble the shelving structure.
